subtype: Approach: reviewing results after a trial change [Revision]
passage: Two months after Aparna dropped two of her four batches at the town coaching centre, she sat on the roof with her cousin Sabina and a page divided in half: BEFORE and NOW. Test scores: 48, 52, 50 before; 61 and 64 now. Sleep: lights out past one, then ten-thirty. Mood: crying on the bus, then humming on the bus. “Could be luck,” Sabina said. “Then we keep it another two months and see,” Aparna answered. Downstairs her mother had wondered aloud whether to bring the batches back. The page settled it. Aparna tucked it under her pencil box, wanting to show it at dinner, and quietly happy that the quiet evenings were hers.

qa.q: What were Aparna's test scores after the change?
What might Aparna be feeling as she compares the two columns?
qa.a: Quiet pride and relief that the lighter schedule is working.

qa.q: What else could Aparna do to strengthen the review, and why?
qa.a: Compare a few more tests before deciding for good, since Sabina says it could be luck and more results would make the decision safer.

qa.q: How does the change look to Aparna's mother?
qa.a: Aparna's mother wondered about bringing the batches back, so the page gives her evidence and she may feel reassured that the lighter plan is working.

grounding: After two months with fewer batches, a student compares scores, sleep and mood and keeps the lighter schedule.

subtype: Approach: reviewing results after a trial change [Revision]
passage:
In Nairobi, Rafael had dropped from four tuition classes to two in September, as a trial agreed with his mother, Wanjiru. Now it was the end of November, and they sat at the kitchen table with his school reports and the notebook he'd kept.

"Before," he said, turning pages. "Maths tests: 54, 56, 55. After: 61, 66, 70."

Wanjiru nodded slowly. "And sleep?"

"Before, about five and a half hours. Now nearly eight. And look," he pointed to a column he'd added himself: mood from one to five. "Before, mostly twos. Now mostly fours."

"You were grumpy," Wanjiru admitted, laughing. "Every morning."

"So can we keep it at two?"

She looked at the numbers again, then at him. "Yes. But we check again at Easter."

Rafael grinned and closed the notebook. He'd expected an argument. The numbers had done the arguing.

qa.q: What were Rafael's maths test scores after the change?
How did Rafael feel when his mother agreed?
qa.a: He felt relieved and pleased, having expected an argument.

qa.q: What else could Rafael track before the Easter check?
qa.a: He could note how much time he spends on self-study, to see which part of the new routine is helping most.

qa.q: How does the review look to Wanjiru?
qa.a: Wanjiru seems convinced and a bit amused, admitting he was grumpy before and seeing clear improvement in the numbers.

grounding: Shows a student comparing test scores, sleep and mood before and after fewer classes, seeing better scores and energy and keeping the lighter schedule.

subtype: Approach: reviewing results after a trial change [Revision]
passage:
In the school library, Nitin spread two sheets on the table in front of his class teacher, Mrs. Shreya Nair. Two months ago, in this same room, she'd helped him convince his parents to let him drop one of his three coaching batches as a trial.

"So?" she asked.

"Test scores first," Nitin said. "Before: physics 48, 51, 49. After: 55, 59, 62."

"Sleep?"

"Before, I slept at one. Now around eleven. I'm not dozing in first period anymore."

"And how do you feel?"

Nitin thought. "Less panicky. I actually understand what I'm solving."

Mrs. Nair smiled. "Then what's your decision?"

"Keep it at two batches. Until the board exams, at least."

She wrote a short note for his parents on school paper: The trial has worked. I support continuing. Nitin folded it into his notebook carefully.

qa.q: What were Nitin's physics scores after the change?
How did Nitin describe his feelings after two months?
qa.a: He said he felt less panicky and actually understood what he was solving.

qa.q: What else could Nitin do to keep the lighter schedule working?
qa.a: He could keep checking his scores and sleep every month, so any drop is caught early and discussed with his parents.

qa.q: How might Mrs. Nair see the trial's result?
qa.a: Mrs. Nair seems pleased and supportive, writing a note for his parents because the evidence shows the change helped.

grounding: Shows a student comparing test scores, sleep and mood before and after a trial with fewer batches, seeing improvement and keeping the lighter schedule.
